questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.stem: What is the integral of 2x times (x^2 + 1)^3 dx? Report the value of the antiderivative evaluated at x=1, assuming C=0.
questions.explanation: Substitute u = x^2 + 1, so du = 2x dx, and the integral becomes the integral of u cubed du, which is u to the fourth over 4. At x = 1, u = 2, giving 16/4 = 4. Using u cubed over 3 would be the integral of u squared, and forgetting the substitution entirely would leave 2x in the integrand.
